record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE reconstruction fidelity and feature changes in Pythia-70m, finding that sparsity-penalized SAEs suppress features and do not perfectly reconstruct activations. It tests whether SAE features are complete and stable, but does not test superposition geometry or polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The results concern SAE reconstruction and feature scaling in Pythia-70m. The single-feature derivation is theoretical, not a test of overlapping features or superposition geometry. The cited Pythia-70m perplexity result from Cunningham et al. is not this study's result. Figure-only layer trends without tabulated values are not separately recorded where the appendix provides layer-wise metrics.
record.test_reason: Mostly a methods post on fixing SAE feature suppression. Its measurements of the pretrained SAEs bear on V5's completeness claim. In Pythia-70m, the L2 ratio is 0.84–0.995, MSE is nonzero, and patched perplexity is 61–94 against about 38 for the unpatched model. The L1 penalty systematically shrinks feature activations. It does not test feature recovery (V4), toy geometry, polysemanticity or dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the L1 sparsity penalty suppresses SAE features, mainly those with frequent but weak activations. Adding a scaling factor and fine-tuning the decoder without the penalty yields ~9% lower MSE and ~24% perplexity-gap recovery without changing when features activate. Scale-only fine-tuning gives 6% and 16%. They recommend correcting suppression before patching SAEs into forward passes.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on Pythia-70m activations and then fine-tunes selected SAE parameters to address feature suppression; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and feature properties matter: reconstruction ratios vary by layer, and feature scaling correlates with activation strength and frequency. Encoder fine-tuning methods drastically reduce sparsity, unlike the decoder-focused methods reported in the main comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder-only fine-tuning without L1 cuts MSE by ~9% and the perplexity gap by ~24% while leaving L0 unchanged. Decoder vectors rotate little (mean cosine 0.983).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature-activation shrinkage from the L1 penalty can be partly corrected post hoc without changing which features fire.

record.problems: Evidence is from one model family member, Pythia-70m, and one training dataset. Several layer-wise trends are presented in figures; the reported correlations are restricted to layer 5 and exclude dead features. No ground-truth feature set is used to establish completeness or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported values for Baseline, Scale, Unrotated Decoder, or encoder-fine-tuning methods are included because they are comparisons of alternative fine-tuning procedures rather than the main pretrained-versus-Decoder reconstruction and feature-stability results. Figure-only per-layer values are not extracted where the appendix table supplies numeric metrics.

untested.parts: No toy model, superposition geometry or sparsity transition.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No test of whether SAE features are interpretable, recover ground truth, or spread across neurons. Reconstruction error alone does not bear on it.
Canonicality and stability across seeds, dictionary sizes or models are untested. Only one SAE size (2048) and one L1 coefficient are used, on Pythia-70m.

missing.what: Dead-feature counts per layer for pretrained SAEs (6 to 422 of 2048 never activate), relevant to dictionary completeness.
Original-model perplexity (~38 on the OpenWebText slice) is needed as the completeness baseline for R7–R12. It appears only in the author's comment reply.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a mitigation/methods post. Only the pretrained-SAE measurements bear on the claim, via V5 completeness. The single-feature derivation is theoretical. The Cunningham et al. perplexity figure in the TL;DR is cited, not this study's result, and is correctly excluded. The V4 links in the record were removed, since imperfect reconstruction does not test whether sparse features exist.

versions.untested_parts: No test of more features than dimensions, overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent geometric transition, or regular superposition geometry.
No test of neuron polysemanticity, feature competition for capacity, or dedication of dimensions to important features.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE reconstruction fidelity only in Pythia-70m; it does not establish ground-truth feature recovery, feature distribution across neurons, or generality to other models.
Tests reconstruction fidelity and some feature stability under decoder fine-tuning, not whether SAE features are canonical units or complete across models and settings.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Pretrained L1 SAEs (2048 features, c=2e-3) on Pythia-70m residual stream, layers 1–6
relationships.reason: SAE reconstructions are incomplete and systematically shrunk. Pretrained L2 ratio is 0.84–0.87 in layers 1–5 (R1–R6, R19–R23). Patched perplexity is 61–94 vs ~38 for the unpatched model (R7–R12). Suppression depends on feature strength and frequency (R25–R32).
relationships.display_finding: Reconstructions were incomplete and systematically shrunk (L2 ratio 0.84–0.87 in layers 1–5), patched perplexity was 61–94 vs about 38 unpatched, and suppression depended on feature strength and frequency.

relationships.condition: Layer 6 pretrained SAE, norm measure only
relationships.reason: The L2 ratio is 0.995, so there is essentially no norm suppression (R24). Patched perplexity is still elevated (R12).
relationships.display_finding: The L2 ratio was 0.995, so norms were barely suppressed, but perplexity with the SAE patched in was still elevated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The SAEs reconstruct activations only imperfectly: reconstruction MSE is nonzero and patched perplexity remains elevated, though decoder fine-tuning improves both (R1–R12, R19–R24). The study does not verify recovered features against ground truth.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported reconstruction errors and sub-unit reconstruction norm ratios show that the pretrained SAE representations do not fully reconstruct activations (R1–R6, R19–R24); the text also reports a substantial perplexity increase when reconstructions are patched in (R7–R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Decoder-fine-tuned SAEs and layer-5 feature scaling
reader_labels.reason: Decoder fine-tuning reduces but does not eliminate reconstruction error in most layers, and feature scaling varies with activation strength and frequency; feature-vector cosine similarity is high on average but some features rotate more (R1–R6, R19–R24, R25–R33).
